title: Shadow stream budgeting and tenant fallback control-plane
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a safe, observable, and tenant-aware way to run shadow (duplicate) requests for canary/A-B/model-eval traffic without uncontrolled cost or noisy cross-tenant interference. Current ad-hoc mirroring spikes spend for a small set of tenants and lacks per-tenant caps, circuit-breakers, or cost accounting.

Goal: Implement a control-plane and enforcement layer that: 1) enforces per-tenant (and global) shadow budgets, 2) provides dynamic sampling and weighted streaming to prioritize high-signal tenants, 3) isolates shadow execution context (no leaks to metrics or billing), and 4) supports safe automatic fallback (stop duplicating) when budget thresholds, latency regressions, or error budgets are breached.

Scope: gateway-level sampling + async enqueuer for mirrored requests; control-plane API for budgets and sampling policies; per-tenant accounting for duplicate-cost attribution; automatic circuit-breaker and fallback policy; dashboard and alerts; e2e canary plan for 3 pilot tenants.

Non-goals: implementing full-fledged A/B traffic splitting for production (this ticket covers only shadow duplication flow and control).

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Sampling granularity: request-level random sampling vs. cohort-based stratified sampling. We chose hybrid stratified sampling (tenant + route) to ensure statistical coverage from low-traffic tenants while preventing large tenants from dominating mirrored budgets.
- Duplication path: synchronous duplicate forwarding vs async fanout. We selected async fanout (gateway -> mirror-enqueue -> mirror-worker pool) to avoid added tail latency to production traffic and allow backpressure control.
- Cost enforcement location: gateway vs runtime. Implement enforcement in the gateway control-plane for immediate rejection of duplications that would exceed budgets; mirror-workers will perform accounting and can stop pulling when limits reached.
- Consistency vs availability: we allow eventual consistency of budget counters (bounded by 3s) to avoid gateway latency amplification.

Telemetry & observability: expose metrics per-tenant and per-route: shadow_rate, shadow_cost_estimate, shadow_budget_remaining, mirror_enqueue_latency, mirror_worker_errors, mirror_retries. Add tracing tags: shadow=true, mirror_policy_id, budget_check_result. Add dashboards and alerts for budget-exhaustion and unexpected cost spikes.

Privacy/safety: mirror requests must be redacted and tagged; do not route PII-sensitive routes to mirrors by default. Access to mirrored payloads requires elevated console permissions. This is enforced by the control-plane policy.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gate, DB-backed control-plane entries for budgets, pilot with 3 tenants (internal+2 customers), monitor cost for two weeks, enable auto-rollback to disable duplication for tenant if cost > X% of committed budget or mirror error rate > 2%.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway can evaluate and enforce per-tenant shadow budget before enqueueing duplicate requests
Mirror-enqueue path is async and does not add >1ms median latency to production request path
Per-tenant cost accounting appears in billing debug logs and dashboard within 60 seconds
Circuit-breaker disables duplication for tenant when budget or error thresholds exceeded and emits alerts
Unit and integration tests for sampling and budget enforcement with 95% coverage for control-plane logic
End-to-end canary executed with 3 pilot tenants and documented results in Confluence

notes: Keep conservative defaults: global shadow_rate cap of 5% and tenant default cap of 1% unless customer opts into higher. Budget units expressed in approximate token-cost-equivalents for cross-model accounting.
implementation_decisions: Use Redis counters with sharded keys for fast budget checks; accept eventual consistency with 3s TTL and reconcile via periodic batch. Mirror-workers will be able to query a synced policy cache to respect runtime changes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: large tenant could exhaust global mirror budget. Mitigation: enforce global headroom and immediate per-tenant throttle plus exponential backoff. Risk: billing attribution mismatch. Mitigation: shadow requests include signed attribution header and mirror-workers log cost receipts to billing topic.
